prompt.context: Insuraco is a large US insurer that's looking to grow. They currently sell a wide range of insurance products to US consumers and are considering developing a new product: $5/month smartphone insurance for under-30s. Insuraco's management is excited about the opportunity of selling to this large, under-insured group.
prompt.question: Before they develop the idea further, Insuraco would like to know: (1) Is this a good idea? and (2) If so, how should they roll out this new product?

clarifying_info.a: To maximize profit, particularly in the first year the product is released.

clarifying_info.q: How does Insuraco currently sell its products?
Which geographies is Insuraco interested in?
clarifying_info.a: The US only. They are licensed to sell in all US states.

clarifying_info.q: Should we include investment income in financial calculations?
clarifying_info.a: No, investment income can be ignored.

exhibits.title: Insuraco's Potential Distribution Channels – 1st Year Projections
exhibits.shows: A table comparing two distribution channels (Website vs. Agents) across four metrics: Development Costs, Year 1 expected website visits/agent enquiries, Conversion Rate, and Combined Ratio. Also notes that average contract length at end of first year is 6 months and Insuraco will only invest in one channel for this product.
exhibits.data: Website: Development Costs $100,000 | Visits 600,000 | Conversion Rate 20.0% | Combined Ratio 97.5%. Agents: Development Costs $50,000 | Enquiries 400,000 | Conversion Rate 12.5% | Combined Ratio 95.0%. Average contract length at end of year 1: 6 months. Insuraco will only invest in one channel.

exhibits.title: Combined Ratio Definition
exhibits.shows: A formula defining the Combined Ratio as Total Costs (i.e. Claims and Operating Expenses) divided by Total Revenue (i.e. Premium). Note: does not include Development Costs.
exhibits.data: Combined Ratio = Total Costs (Claims & Operating Expenses) / Total Revenue (Premium). Does not include Development Costs.

framework: Is the market attractive? — Size & Growth: estimate the annual revenue of the US under-30s smartphone insurance market
Is the market attractive? — Competition: assess the competitive landscape
Is the market attractive? — Customers: understand buying preferences and which distribution channel resonates
Can Insuraco enter effectively? — Product: evaluate the $5/month offering and coverage terms
Can Insuraco enter effectively? — Capabilities: assess Insuraco's pricing expertise, brand strength, and channel options

questions.prompt: Estimate the annual revenue of the US under-30s smartphone insurance market.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a top-down funnel: US population → % under 30 → % owning a smartphone → % interested in smartphone insurance → % willing to pay → annual premium per customer. Reasoning and structure matter more than the exact answer. A result around $100m is acceptable.

math.setup: US Population x % under 30 x % owning a smartphone x % interested x % willing to pay x annual premium per customer
steps: % under 30: life expectancy ~80 years, equal age distribution → 30/80 ≈ 37.5%, round to ~35% → ~112m people under 30
% owning a smartphone: 0% for under-15s, ~80% for 15-to-30-year-olds → ~40% overall → ~45m
% interested in smartphone insurance: low adoption in this group → ~20% → ~9m

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the first-year profit of each distribution channel (Website vs. Agents).
questions.guidance: Candidate must understand the Combined Ratio (present Exhibit 2 if asked), derive profit margin as (1 – Combined Ratio), apply the 6-month average contract length, and subtract one-time development costs. Both channels yield a first-year profit of $25k after the website investment uplift is revealed.

math.setup: Paying customers = visits/enquiries x conversion rate. Annual revenue per customer = $5/month x 6 months (avg contract length in yr 1). Profit per customer = revenue per customer x (1 – Combined Ratio). Total operating profit = paying customers x profit per customer. Net profit = total operating profit – development costs.
steps: WEBSITE (base case): Customers = 600k x 20% = 120k. Revenue/customer = $5 x 6 = $30. Profit/customer = $30 x 2.5% (1-97.5%) = $0.75. Operating profit = 120k x $0.75 = $90k. Net profit = $90k - $100k = -$10k.
AGENTS: Customers = 400k x 12.5% = 50k. Revenue/customer = $5 x 6 = $30. Profit/customer = $30 x 5% (1-95%) = $1.50. Operating profit = 50k x $1.50 = $75k. Net profit = $75k - $50k = $25k.

WEBSITE (with 10% cost increase → conversion rate 30%): Development costs = $100k x 1.10 = $110k. Customers = 600k x 30% = 180k. Operating profit = 180k x $0.75 = $135k. Net profit = $135k - $110k = $25k.
Both channels now yield $25k in year 1.

Long-run: Development costs are one-time, so the website becomes more profitable after year 1 because it signs up more customers. An average contract length of ~3 years further amplifies website profitability over time.
math.answer: Both channels: $25k net profit in year 1. Website preferred in the long run due to one-time development costs and higher customer volume.

brainstorming.prompt: What other non-financial considerations need to be addressed in rolling out this new product?

categories.name: Marketing & Branding
ideas: How can Insuraco make insurance relevant, cool, and desirable to under-30s?
Does Insuraco have the marketing capability for this demographic, or does it need to hire new expertise?
Should Insuraco create a new sub-brand rather than selling under its existing brand?

categories.name: Agent Relationship Management
ideas: Insuraco currently sells all products through agents — will launching a direct website channel endanger those relationships?
How should Insuraco communicate the new channel strategy to its agent network?

categories.name: Competitor Response
ideas: The product is easily replicable (home/contents insurers already offer smartphone coverage); how does Insuraco differentiate?
What barriers to entry can Insuraco build (brand loyalty, switching costs, pricing)?

categories.name: Growth Opportunities
ideas: Could this product open the door to other under-30s products (travel insurance, renters insurance, auto insurance)?
How can Insuraco foster brand loyalty early to become the insurer of choice for larger policies later in life (homeowners, life, medical)?
Cross-sell and upsell potential within the under-30 cohort.

recommendation: Insuraco should launch the $5/month smartphone insurance product for under-30s via a website, targeting a first-year profit of $25k (with 30% conversion at $110k development cost).
The market is large (~$100m annual revenue), currently competitor-free, and profitable (Combined Ratio below 100% in both channels).

The website is the preferred channel because development costs are a one-time expense, it acquires more customers, and long-term profitability (especially with an expected ~3-year contract length) exceeds the agent channel.
risks: Future number of website visits and agent enquiries is unknown; profitability projections are sensitive to traffic levels.
Combined Ratios and Conversion Rates may not remain constant as the market matures or competitors enter.
Launching a direct website channel could strain existing agent relationships.
next_steps: Conduct market research to understand future trends in website visits and agent enquiries.
Develop a marketing and branding strategy tailored to under-30s.
Manage and communicate with the existing agent network to protect those relationships.
Monitor competitor response and develop differentiation strategy.
Explore adjacent product opportunities (travel, renters, auto) to capitalize on the under-30 customer relationship.
